accepted.s: According to the Agricultural Census 2015-16, what proportion of total operational holdings and operated area respectively was accounted for by small and marginal holdings below 2 hectares?
accepted.x: Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of all holdings but accounted for only 47.3% of the operated area in 2015-16.
accepted.tq: Read the table row-wise and distinguish the share of holdings from the share of operated area.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Agricultural Census 2015-16:
1. Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of the holdings.
2. Semi-medium and medium holdings accounted for 43.6% of the operated area.
3. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 43.6% of the total holdings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Semi-medium and medium holdings constituted 13.2% of holdings, not 43.6%; 43.6% was their share of operated area.
accepted.tq: Separate percentages referring to holdings from those referring to operated area.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the Agricultural Census 2010-11, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 58% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 58% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 85% of holdings and held about 44% of operated area.
Small holdings constituted about 44% of holdings and held about 85% of operated area.
accepted.x: In the 2010-11 Agricultural Census, small holdings were about 85% of holdings but accounted for only about 44% of the operated area.
accepted.tq: Match the two percentages with their correct dimensions instead of reversing the table.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about agricultural holdings in India:
1. There were about 146 million holdings in 2015-16.
2. The average size of a holding was about 1.08 hectares in 2015-16.
3. The 11th Agriculture Census 2021-22 has, so far, only provisional State results.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: India had about 146 million holdings averaging 1.08 hectares in 2015-16, while only provisional State results of the 2021-22 Census were available as stated.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and status statement independently before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the provisional 11th Agriculture Census data for Andhra Pradesh, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.94 hectares; number of holdings—96.90 lakh
Average holding size—0.86 hectares; number of holdings—85.24 lakh
Average holding size—1.08 hectares; number of holdings—146 million
accepted.x: The provisional Andhra Pradesh figures are an average holding size of 0.86 hectares and 96.90 lakh holdings, compared with 0.94 hectares and 85.24 lakh holdings in 2015-16.
accepted.tq: Use the sure numerical pair and reject options that mix figures from different years or geographical levels.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a reason for the poor viability of small and marginal agricultural holdings?
accepted.x: Small and marginal holdings are associated with few surpluses, not abundant marketable surpluses. Uneconomical mechanisation, weak bargaining power and poor credit are identified viability constraints.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated condition rather than merely naming a related problem.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following measures is most directly intended to improve the viability and bargaining position of small and marginal farmers by aggregating them into producer organisations?
o: Reduction of operated area per holding
Replacement of crop insurance by informal lending
accepted.x: Farmer Producer Organisations aggregate farmers and improve their collective bargaining and economic position. The other alternatives would weaken, rather than improve, viability.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional remedy that addresses fragmentation and weak bargaining power.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Central Sector scheme for formation and promotion of how many Farmer Producer Organisations was launched in 2020, with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore?
accepted.x: The 10,000 FPO scheme was launched in 2020 with an outlay of ₹6,865 crore.
accepted.tq: Use the scheme’s distinctive target number and expenditure together.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As reported up to January 2026, how many farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
accepted.x: By January 2026, 56.32 lakh farmers had been registered under the 10,000 FPO scheme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish lakh-level registration data from the number of holdings and the scheme target.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following set of measures is associated with improving the viability of small and marginal holdings?
o: Reduction of irrigation and removal of collective institutions
Exclusive dependence on individual machinery ownership and informal credit
Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming
Abolition of producer organisations and cluster-based activities
accepted.x: Custom Hiring Centres, cluster farming and cooperative or joint farming are identified as remedies for the viability constraints of small holdings.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of stated institutional and operational remedies.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding cooperative joint farming in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: There are 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while their federations are under liquidation.
There are 10,000 primary societies functioning under the FPO scheme.
There are 85.24 primary societies, while federations are being expanded.
There are 210 federations, while all primary societies have been dissolved.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 210 primary Cooperative Joint Farming Societies, while the federations are under liquidation as reported for 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Match the correct institutional level with the correct status instead of swapping societies and federations.
accepted.sec: Small and marginal holdings viability - holdings vs operated area, collective farming, FPOs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal source for official data on farmer and agricultural labourer suicides in India is which of the following?
o: Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households
Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India
accepted.x: The National Crime Records Bureau publishes the report titled “Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India” (ADSI), which is the cited source for these suicide data.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact official report title rather than a related agricultural publication.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NCRB ADSI 2015 data, the biggest reported cause of farmer suicides was:
accepted.x: The biggest cause identified in the NCRB ADSI 2015 data was bankruptcy or indebtedness.
accepted.tq: Recall the principal causal category and avoid substituting a general agricultural problem for the recorded cause.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the regional pattern of farmer suicides:
1. A 28-year NCRB analysis covered the period 1995-2023.
2. The analysis found a sharp resurgence in suicides in 2023 after a decade of decline.
3. Suicides have been concentrated mainly in rain-fed belts.
4. Historically, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh have been among the most severely affected areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the reported time span, recent resurgence, rain-fed concentration and historical concentration in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Combine temporal, geographical and state-level clues only after checking each statement.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to NCRB ADSI 2024, the total number of suicides reported in India and the number attributed to the farm sector respectively were:
accepted.x: ADSI 2024 reported 1,70,746 suicides in total, of which 10,546 belonged to the farm sector.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the aggregate total from the farm-sector subset.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The farm-sector suicide figure of 10,546 in NCRB ADSI 2024 comprised:
o: 10,546 farmers or cultivators and no agricultural labourers
4,481 farmers or cultivators and 152 agricultural labourers
4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers
5,913 farmers or cultivators and 4,633 agricultural labourers
accepted.x: The farm-sector total consisted of 4,633 farmers or cultivators and 5,913 agricultural labourers.
accepted.tq: Break the aggregate into its two component categories before selecting the option.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What percentage of total suicides did the farm sector account for in NCRB ADSI 2024?
accepted.x: The farm sector accounted for 10,546 out of 1,70,746 suicides, reported as 6.2% of the total.
accepted.tq: Link the percentage to the stated total and subset rather than to one component alone.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the gender-wise distribution of farmer or cultivator suicides in NCRB ADSI 2024, which one of the following is correct?
accepted.x: Of the farmer or cultivator suicides, 4,481 were men and 152 were women.
accepted.tq: Keep the farmer or cultivator category separate from the broader farm-sector total.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the reported position regarding farmer and tenant suicides in Andhra Pradesh under the coalition government?
o: The Tenant Farmers Association reported over 300 deaths, while 112 were officially recognised.
The Association reported 112 deaths, while over 300 were officially recognised.
No deaths were reported and no demand for an inquiry was made.
Both the Association and official records reported exactly 300 deaths.
accepted.x: The Tenant Farmers Association claimed that more than 300 farmers and tenants died by suicide, whereas only 112 were officially recognised. It demanded a truth-finding committee.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an association’s claim from the number officially recognised.
accepted.sec: Farmer suicides - NCRB ADSI data, causes, states, AP position  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the work of the National Commission on Farmers?
o: It was set up exclusively for food procurement and submitted one report in 2015.
It was set up to regulate foreign trade and submitted five reports during 1991-1996.
It was set up to formulate industrial policy and submitted two reports during 2007-2010.
It was set up to address the calamity of farmer suicides and submitted five reports during 2004-2006.
accepted.x: The Commission was established to address the crisis of farmer suicides and submitted five reports between 2004 and 2006.
accepted.tq: Match the Commission’s purpose with its correct number and period of reports.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
C2, in the MSP formula recommended by the National Commission on Farmers, includes which of the following components?
1. A2 costs
2. Imputed value of family labour
3. Imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: C2 includes A2, family labour and imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital; hence all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Expand the cost acronym component by component before judging the statements.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Commission’s MSP recommendation from the formula applied by the Government?
o: The Commission recommended C2 plus 50%, while the Government applies 50% over A2+FL.
The Commission recommended A2+FL plus 50%, while the Government applies C2 plus 50%.
The Commission recommended C2 minus 50%, while the Government applies A2 alone.
Both the Commission and the Government apply only C2 without any margin.
accepted.x: The Commission recommended C2 plus 50%, whereas the Government applies 50% over A2+FL, which does not include the full C2 cost concept.
accepted.tq: Split the similar-looking formulas at the cost base—C2 versus A2+FL.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the recommendations associated with the National Commission on Farmers?
o: Secure rights for women and tenants
accepted.x: The Commission recommended affordable credit, not its abolition. It also recommended land reforms, rights for women and tenants, universal crop insurance and a National Agricultural Risk Fund.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reverses a recommendation by using an institutional opposite.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the recommendations and vision of the National Commission on Farmers:
1. It supported land reforms and market reforms.
2. It recommended irrigation, cheaper institutional credit and crop insurance.
3. It envisaged farming as economically viable and ecologically sustainable.
4. It sought improvement in the quality of life of farmers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements reflect the Commission’s recommendations and core vision for economically viable, ecologically sustainable farming and improved farmer welfare.
accepted.tq: Group the policy recommendations with the Commission’s broader outcome-oriented vision.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of which body?
o: Agricultural Costs and Prices Commission alone
accepted.x: The National Policy for Farmers, 2007 drew upon the reports of the National Commission on Farmers chaired by M. S. Swaminathan.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy-report linkage by matching the policy with the body that prepared the relevant recommendations.
accepted.sec: National Commission on Farmers (Swaminathan) - year, reports, MSP formula  [APPSC]
